title: Design an Ad Click Aggregator / Real-Time Analytics
relevance: High — canonical “scaling writes + stream processing” HLD (Alex Xu Vol.2 ch.6 / Hello Interview); Meta, Google, Amazon, Uber, Netflix ads; probes Kafka/Flink, windowed aggregation, dedup/idempotency, Lambda vs Kappa, OLAP serving.
company_notes: Campus/intern/new-grad: Kafka buffer, pre-agg, OLAP, basic dedup, why not one SQL table. Experienced / Meta–Google–Uber ads: event-time windows, hot shards, Lambda vs Kappa, impression signing, peak write QPS, billing vs dashboard accuracy. Top-tier HLD alongside metrics/Top-K/notifications; depth is write scaling + stream correctness, not auction or fraud ML unless asked.

phases.goal: Lock functional scope, NFRs, and what is explicitly out of scope before designing.

must_hit.point: In scope: record clicks (often impressions), redirect to advertiser URL, query aggregates by ad/campaign over time with ≥1-minute granularity, optional geo/device slices, near-real-time dashboard freshness.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists click/impression recording, redirect, minute-grain metrics, optional dimensions, and freshness as in-scope.

must_hit.point: Out of scope unless pulled: ad targeting/auction/RTB, creative CDN, full fraud ML, cross-device identity, conversion attribution.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly parks auction, CDN, fraud ML, identity, and attribution.

must_hit.point: NFRs: peak write throughput; no silent click loss after accept; sub-second reads on pre-agg; freshness seconds–minutes; idempotent counting; billing accuracy stricter than dashboard freshness.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates durability, read latency on pre-agg, freshness, idempotency, and billing vs dashboard bar.

must_hit.point: Clarify clicks-only vs impressions+clicks, dimensions, freshness SLA, billing vs dashboard, and logged-in users only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks clarifying questions on event types, dims, SLAs, and billing path.

probes: What is in scope vs out of scope, and how do dashboard freshness and billing accuracy differ?

hints.1: Start with what the system must record and what queries advertisers need.
hints.2: Separate functional (track, redirect, aggregate) from NFRs and name what you will not design.
hints.3: Say ≥1-minute aggregates, near-real-time dashboards, no silent loss after accept, and billing stricter than dashboard; park RTB/fraud/attribution.

phases.goal: Align write-heavy scale and show why pre-aggregation beats scanning raw events.

must_hit.point: Hello Interview baseline: 10M active ads, peak ~10k clicks/s; if peak ≈ 10× average → ~1k/s avg → ~100M clicks/day.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States 10M ads, ~10k/s peak, ~1k/s avg, ~100M clicks/day with the 10× peak/avg link.

must_hit.point: Event size ~100–500 B → raw ingest tens of MB/s peak; retention (e.g. 7–30d Kafka + longer lake) dominates storage more than OLAP rollups.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses 100–500 B events, tens of MB/s peak, and 7–30d Kafka plus lake retention as the storage driver.

must_hit.point: Pre-agg shrinks data hard: 86400 minutes/day × ads × dims ≪ raw events if only non-zero buckets are stored; dashboard reads ≪ write path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts 86400 minute buckets and non-zero-only storage with raw volume, and notes reads are secondary.

probes: Walk through peak click rate, daily volume, and why we optimize writes and pre-agg first.

hints.1: Pick a peak click QPS and relate it to average and daily volume.
hints.2: Use the 10M ads / ~10k clicks/s baseline and convert peak to daily clicks.
hints.3: State ~10k/s peak, ~100M clicks/day, 100–500 B events, 7–30d retention, and that pre-agg and write path dominate over dashboard QPS.

phases.goal: Define click/event intake and metrics query interfaces including redirect and auth.

must_hit.point: GET /v1/click with ad_id, impression_id, sig → validate → enqueue → 302 to advertiser landing URL.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes signed click GET that enqueues then 302 redirects.

must_hit.point: Alternate beacon POST /v1/events with event_id, type click|impression, ad_id, campaign_id, event_time, dims → 202 for mobile SDKs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions async POST /v1/events returning 202.

must_hit.point: GET metrics on ads/campaigns with from/to, granularity 1m|1h|1d, group_by country/device; public/signed click URL vs authenticated advertiser metrics; billing export consumes reconciled aggregates only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows metrics GETs with granularity/group_by, auth split, and reconciled-only billing export.

probes: How does the click URL work end-to-end, and how do advertisers query metrics?

hints.1: Think tracking endpoint first, then a separate read API for dashboards.
hints.2: Click path should validate and enqueue before redirect; metrics are authenticated queries over time ranges.
hints.3: GET /v1/click → enqueue → 302; optional POST /v1/events → 202; GET .../metrics with 1m|1h|1d; billing webhook only on reconciled aggregates.

phases.goal: Model raw events, dedup state, OLAP aggregates, lake truth, and billing snapshots.

must_hit.point: Raw impression/click event: event_id or impression_id, ad_id, campaign_id, advertiser_id, optional user_id, event_time, ingest_time, ip/ua hashes, country, device, HMAC sig.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the raw event fields including dual timestamps and HMAC sig.

must_hit.point: Dedup store: Redis set / Bloom of impression_id with TTL ≈ attribution window (hours–days); OLAP aggregate fact keyed by ad_id, window_start, granularity, dims → clicks, impressions, optional unique_approx.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates impression_id dedup with TTL from OLAP fact keys and counts.

must_hit.point: Raw lake Parquet/ORC on S3/GCS as source of truth for batch recompute; billing snapshot as immutable daily/hourly exact counts post-reconciliation with audited corrections.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names lake as batch source of truth and immutable reconciled billing snapshots.

probes: What do you store raw vs pre-aggregated, and where does dedup state live?

hints.1: You need both an append-only event record and something dashboards can query quickly.
hints.2: Split raw event, dedup set/Bloom, OLAP minute facts, lake, and billing snapshots.
hints.3: Raw event with impression_id/HMAC; Redis/Bloom TTL hours–days; OLAP (ad_id, window_start, dims)→counts; lake Parquet for Spark; immutable reconciled billing rows.

phases.goal: Assemble intake → Kafka → Flink windows → OLAP, plus batch reconcile for billing.

must_hit.point: Click/Event API behind LB: verify HMAC, dedup, append to Kafka clicks topic keyed by ad_id or salted key, archive to lake, then 302; Ad Placement Service is a black box issuing signed impression_id + click URL.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes stateless click API: HMAC, dedup, Kafka produce, lake archive, 302 after durable accept.

must_hit.point: Flink event-time tumbling windows emit minute aggregates to OLAP (Pinot/Druid/ClickHouse/BigQuery); Spark batch reconciler does exact dedup/aggregate from lake for billing and OLAP correction.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Flink minute windows to OLAP and Spark lake reconcile for authoritative billing.

must_hit.point: Happy path freshness is about window + checkpoint lag; optional Redis hot counters for pacing/budget and a fraud filter before count.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties dashboard lag to window/checkpoint and mentions optional pacing Redis and fraud filter.

probes: Draw the path from user click to advertiser chart and the separate billing path.

hints.1: Buffer clicks before aggregating; do not write dashboards synchronously from the click handler.
hints.2: API → Kafka → Flink → OLAP for dashboards; lake → Spark for billing truth.
hints.3: HMAC+dedup+Kafka then 302; Flink 1-min event-time windows to OLAP; Spark exact GROUP BY impression_id for invoices; never invoice from provisional stream alone.

phases.goal: Defend Lambda vs Kappa, dedup keys, exactly-once, hot keys, late events, and hierarchical rollups.

must_hit.point: Batch alone is stale under spikes; stream alone is hard to prove money-correct — senior answer is speed layer for UX + batch for truth (Lambda); Kappa if arguing one streaming codebase + log replay.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares batch vs stream and lands on Lambda (speed+batch) or justified Kappa.

must_hit.point: Dedup before windowing with signed per-impression id; user_id+ad_id is wrong for retargeting; Bloom FPs can drop real clicks — prefer exact Redis on money-adjacent paths.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on signed impression_id dedup before windows and calls out Bloom FP risk for billing.

must_hit.point: Exactly-once story: Flink checkpoints + Kafka transactions + idempotent sink (e.g. Pinot upsert); honest shorthand is at-least-once + idempotent aggregate key.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Does not claim naked EOS; cites checkpoints, Kafka transactions, idempotent sink.

must_hit.point: Hot ads: salt ad_id then merge with SUM upsert or query-time sum; late events via watermark + allowed lateness, then side-output corrections or batch reconcile; long-range queries use hour/day rollups.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Covers salting, watermarks/lateness, and hierarchical hour/day pre-agg.

probes: Would you use Lambda or Kappa for billing-grade counts, and how do you dedupe and handle hot ads?

hints.1: Separate dashboard freshness from invoice correctness.
hints.2: Talk speed vs batch layers, where dedup runs, and what happens when one ad goes viral.
hints.3: Lambda: Flink→OLAP for UX, Spark over lake for money; signed impression_id before windows; salt hot ad_id; watermarks for late mobile events; hour/day rollups for long ranges.

phases.goal: Scale each stage and define durable accept, replay, and failure healing.

must_hit.point: Scale Click API horizontally behind LB with a lean verify/dedup/produce/redirect path; Kafka: more partitions, salt popular ads, monitor consumer lag.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Horizontally scales API and addresses Kafka hot keys/partitions and lag.

must_hit.point: Flink keyed state by ad+window; tune checkpoint interval (Uber ~2 min for EOS) vs freshness; dedup Redis sharded by impression_id with TTL so memory stays small; OLAP writes aggregates not every raw click.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions Flink state/checkpoints (~2 min Uber), TTL’d Redis shards, and aggregate-only OLAP writes.

must_hit.point: Durable accept = Kafka ack before 302; replay retained offsets; reconciliation heals stream drift; DLQ for poison events; never block ingest on Spark; multi-region dual produce + union/upsert if active-active.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States Kafka-ack-before-302, replay, reconcile, DLQ, and non-blocking batch.

probes: Where does this system break first at peak write load, and how do you recover from processor bugs?

hints.1: Walk the pipeline and name the first bottleneck on each hop.
hints.2: API QPS, Kafka hot partitions, Flink checkpoints, Redis memory, OLAP write amp, batch overrun.
hints.3: LB-scale lean click handlers; salt Kafka keys; Uber-like ~2 min checkpoints vs freshness; Kafka ack before 302 then replay/reconcile; write aggregates only to OLAP.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Batch alone is simple but stale under spikes; stream alone is fresh but harder to prove money-correct. Prefer speed layer (Flink → near-real-time OLAP) for dashboards and batch (Spark over lake) for billing truth; choose Kappa only if you defend one streaming codebase plus log replay and still have a money-correctness story.

tradeoffs.topic: Dedup timing and key vs Bloom vs Redis
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Dedup before windowing so cross-minute duplicates are not double-counted. Use signed per-impression id, not user_id+ad_id. Bloom is space-cheap but false positives can drop real clicks—prefer exact Redis for money-adjacent paths or accept FP only on non-billing dashboards.

tradeoffs.topic: Exactly-once delivery claim vs at-least-once + idempotent sink
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Do not claim naked exactly-once. Honest interview story is Flink checkpoints + Kafka transactions + idempotent sink (Pinot upsert / UUID), summarized as at-least-once plus idempotent aggregate key.
Millions of ad IDs with multi-dimension slices favor columnar OLAP (Pinot/Druid/ClickHouse); plain TSDB only if cardinality and query shape stay tiny.
Prefer server-side 302 through /click (count then redirect) over client-only navigation/best-effort beacon that can skip tracking and lose revenue.

gotchas.trap: Aggregating in the same OLTP DB that stores raw clicks with GROUP BY at 10k/s.
gotchas.correction: Store raw for audit/replay; serve pre-aggregated rows from OLAP, never COUNT(*) on OLTP at peak write rate.

gotchas.trap: Counting with processing time so late mobile clicks land in the wrong minute.
gotchas.correction: Bucket by event time; use watermarks and allowed lateness so late events join the correct window.

gotchas.trap: Claiming exactly-once without dedup, idempotent sink, or checkpoint story.
gotchas.correction: Explain at-least-once delivery plus Flink checkpoints, Kafka transactions, and idempotent OLAP upsert/aggregate keys.

gotchas.trap: Deduping only inside a 1-minute Flink window.
gotchas.correction: Dedup before windowing (e.g. Redis/Bloom on impression_id) so duplicates across window boundaries do not double-count.

gotchas.trap: Using user_id + ad_id forever as the idempotency key.
gotchas.correction: Use signed per-impression id so legitimate re-shows/retargeting still count correctly.

gotchas.trap: Billing off the real-time layer without batch reconciliation.
gotchas.correction: Invoice from batch-reconciled exact counts over the lake; treat stream aggregates as provisional for dashboards unless product explicitly allows otherwise.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring hot ad partition imbalance after a celebrity campaign.
gotchas.correction: Salt hot ad_id keys across partitions and merge with SUM upsert or query-time sum.
Use server-side 302 tracking after durable enqueue so lost beacons do not silently drop revenue.

gotchas.trap: Building custom stream-state on raw Kafka consumers when asked for seniority.
gotchas.correction: Name Flink/Spark tradeoffs: event-time windows, watermarks, checkpoints, and why plain consumers fail for windowed state.

gotchas.trap: Scope creep into a full fraud platform without being asked.
gotchas.correction: Mention invalid traffic/bots briefly, then park behind a filter service unless the interviewer expands scope.
